title: Identity & scoped access
summary: Enforce allowed actions in credentials and runtime controls.

sections.label: Two meanings of tokens
sections.text: Scoped application tokens authorize API actions. Model tokens measure inference input/output; AI credits are a billing unit. These controls solve different problems.

sections.label: Proposed controls
items: Scope tools and credentials to the assigned task and environment.
Record the identity performing each action, such as a requesting user or a service account. Check the configured actor for tools such as Rovo.
Filter retrieval by access rights before generating output.
Constrain both model-invoked tools and direct workflow code.
Keep code review, data approval, and publication rules executable and attributable.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: An agent cannot exceed its assigned access by following a prompt. Output does not expose evidence inaccessible to the intended reader.

catalog.applicability: Use when assigning tools, credentials and write actions to an agent or workflow step, so that allowed actions are enforced by scoped credentials and runtime controls rather than by the prompt. Record the identity performing each action and filter retrieval by access rights before generating output.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
